title: PRO-LONG: Programmatic Memory Enables Long-Horizon Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2607.20064v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Long-horizon tasks require sustained perception, reasoning, and exploration, and are a persistent challenge for large language model (LLM) agents. This gap is reflected in their limited performance on continual learning benchmarks such as ARC-AGI-3 and NetHack, especially when evaluated without specialized harnesses. Various agent harnesses have been proposed to close the gap, and each commits to a strategy for handling long sequences of observations, i.e., what information to save from the environment and how to load it into model context, a choice we argue is particularly consequential. Existing methods for context management have typically been designed around a tradeoff, where preserving more information makes relevant details harder to retrieve. Recent progress in coding agents, however, makes new approaches to memory viable. We propose PRO-LONG, a minimal context management framework built around programmatic memory for LLM age

translated_title: PRO-LONG：程序化记忆实现长程推理
translated_abstract: 长程任务需要持续的感知、推理和探索，对大型语言模型（LLM）智能体而言始终是一个挑战。这一差距体现在它们在ARC-AGI-3和NetHack等持续学习基准上的有限表现，尤其是在没有专用框架的情况下进行评估时。为了缩小这一差距，已有多种智能体框架被提出，每个框架都采用了一种处理长序列观测的策略，即从环境中保存哪些信息以及如何将其加载到模型上下文中，我们认为这一选择尤为关键。现有的上下文管理方法通常围绕一种权衡而设计：保存更多信息会使相关细节更难检索。然而，编程智能体领域的最新进展使得新的记忆方法成为可能。我们提出了PRO-LONG，一个为LLM智能体构建的、围绕程序化记忆的最小化上下文管理框架。
tldr: 提出PRO-LONG框架，通过程序化记忆为LLM智能体实现长程推理的高效上下文管理，突破了传统方法中信息保存量与检索难度之间的权衡。
en_tdlr: PRO-LONG is a minimal context management framework built around programmatic memory that enables long-horizon reasoning for LLM agents, overcoming the traditional tradeoff between information preservation and retrieval difficulty.
